title: The pancreas sends enzymes and bicarbonate into the small intestine
summary: OpenStax says pancreatic juice digests sugars, proteins, and fats and buffers acid coming from the stomach.
body: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology says the pancreas produces more than a liter of pancreatic juice a day. The juice is mostly water, with salts, sodium bicarbonate, and digestive enzymes. The bicarbonate makes the juice slightly alkaline so it can buffer acidic chyme, inactivate pepsin from the stomach, and give a better setting for enzymes that work in the small intestine. Those enzymes take part in digesting sugars, proteins, and fats. Protein-digesting enzymes are secreted in inactive forms so they do not digest the pancreas itself. This is the 25 April 2013 textbook, paraphrased.
